findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
TrustCertificateActivity (cert4android) is exported with no permission and, when started with EXTRA_TRUSTED, registers a trust decision for the supplied certificate without any user action (processIntent -> registerDecision). Being singleInstance, a second intent via onNewIntent reliably marks an attacker certificate as user-trusted in CustomCertStore, enabling MITM of CalDAV/OkHttp traffic. Other exported activities (UriHandler, MainActivity, FilterSelectionActivity, widget/Tasker config) only show UI to the user or return user-selected values. Ward's analyzer said: Exported activities without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0366: Exported And Unprotected Broadcast Receivers That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
FireReceiver is exported with no permission and creates tasks or posts list notifications from the caller's bundle. Its only check is that intent.getPackage() equals the app's package, which any sender can set, so any app can create tasks, bypassing the WRITE_TASKS permission that guards the API provider. The other exported receivers only react to system actions (boot, package replaced, provider change, widget update) by refreshing state. Ward's analyzer said: Exported receivers without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0337: References to Object Deserialization of Untrusted Data
findings.explanation:
The exported MainActivity (no permission) deserializes a Filter parcelable from the OPEN_FILTER extra and uses it as the task list query. Filter subclasses (e.g. FilterImpl, CustomFilter) carry a raw sql string, so another app can supply arbitrary SQL that runs against the app database, with no validation of the filter type or contents.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:653: MainActivity is exported without a permission.
app/src/main/java/com/todoroo/astrid/activity/MainActivity.kt:671: Untrusted Filter (with its sql) taken from the intent.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0339: SQL Injection in Content Providers
findings.explanation:
TasksContentProvider's todoagenda query concatenates the caller's selection into raw SQL and drops selectionArgs (.create().sql). Any app holding the user-grantable READ_TASKS permission can inject subqueries to read tables beyond the exposed task columns.
app/src/main/java/org/tasks/provider/TasksContentProvider.kt:60: Caller-controlled selection inserted into the query.
app/src/main/java/org/tasks/provider/TasksContentProvider.kt:62: Only the SQL string is used; bind args are discarded before rawQuery.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0208: Insufficient Key Sizes
findings.explanation:
The AndroidKeyStore AES key protecting stored account passwords is generated without setKeySize, so it uses the keystore default of 128 bits, which this test treats as insufficient.
kmp/src/androidMain/kotlin/org/tasks/security/AndroidKeyProvider.kt:27: KeyGenParameterSpec built with no setKeySize (defaults to AES-128).

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0282: Unsafe Custom Trust Evaluation
findings.explanation:
OkHttp clients use cert4android's custom X509TrustManager, which accepts any certificate stored as 'trusted by user', bypassing system/NSC validation. That trust store can be written by any app through the exported TrustCertificateActivity's EXTRA_TRUSTED path, so an attacker-chosen certificate can become trusted.
cert4android/src/androidMain/kotlin/at/bitfire/cert4android/CustomCertStore.kt:103: Any user-trusted cert short-circuits chain validation.
kmp/src/androidMain/kotlin/org/tasks/http/AndroidOkHttpClientFactory.kt:40: Custom trust manager installed for all OkHttp clients.
cert4android/src/androidMain/kotlin/at/bitfire/cert4android/TrustCertificateActivity.kt:101: Trust decision reachable from other apps via exported activity.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0283: Incorrect Implementation of Server Hostname Verification
findings.explanation:
The HostnameVerifier accepts a certificate whose hostname does not match whenever that certificate is in the user-trusted store, and other apps can populate that store through the exported TrustCertificateActivity.
cert4android/src/jvmCommonMain/kotlin/at/bitfire/cert4android/CustomCertManager.kt:75: Bad-hostname certificates explicitly allowed.
cert4android/src/jvmCommonMain/kotlin/at/bitfire/cert4android/CustomCertManager.kt:85: Returns true despite hostname mismatch.

findings.title: MASWE-0030: Improper Use of the Clipboard
findings.explanation:
Generated app passwords (and other account fields) are copied to the clipboard as a plain ClipData without the ClipDescription EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE flag, so they show in clipboard previews and are readable by clipboard-access apps/keyboards.

findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0231: References to Logging APIs
findings.explanation:
Release builds log Microsoft Graph HTTP traffic at HEADERS level via Timber.d; only the Authorization header is sanitized, so Cookie/Set-Cookie headers are logged. In release, FileLogger (a DebugTree) writes all levels to cacheDir/logs, which is zipped into shareable support logs.
